The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Fix observations $y_{1:T}$, a standard-Borel parameter space $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$,
a prior probability $\pi_0$, and the finite-horizon Feynman–Kac path model in
[[def-feynman-kac-path-targets-and-normalizers]]. Write
$$L_\theta(y_{1:T})=\gamma_{\theta,T}(1),\qquad C=\int_\Theta L_\theta(y_{1:T})\,\pi_0(d\theta).$$
Require every prefix normalizer $0<Z_{\theta,t}<\infty$ for $t=0,\ldots,T$
and $\pi_0$-almost every $\theta$, together with $0<C<\infty$; then the
parameter posterior is
$$\pi_y(d\theta)=C^{-1}L_\theta(y_{1:T})\,\pi_0(d\theta).$$

For fixed particle count $N\ge1$, let $U$ contain the full output of
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]] at $\theta$ and a terminal index
$K\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$ drawn conditionally with its final normalized weight.
Let $m_\theta(du)$ be this measurable auxiliary-variable probability kernel and
let $\widehat L_\theta(U)=\widehat Z_T$ be jointly measurable and nonnegative
in $(\theta,U)$. The required interface is
$$\int\widehat L_\theta(u)\,m_\theta(du)=L_\theta(y_{1:T});$$
[[thm-sequential-particle-estimator-is-unbiased]] supplies this identity under
its finite-horizon support and integrability hypotheses. Define the extended
target probability by
$$\widetilde\pi(d\theta,du)=C^{-1}\pi_0(d\theta)m_\theta(du)\widehat L_\theta(u).$$

Given current $(\theta,U)$, propose $\theta'\sim R(\theta,\cdot)$ and then
$U'\sim m_{\theta'}$. Apply the general Metropolis–Hastings construction
[[alg-metropolis-hastings-kernel]] to this proposal kernel and target
$\widetilde\pi$. On rejection retain the entire current pair $(\theta,U)$,
including its stored likelihood estimate and selected path index. When $\pi_0$
and $R$ have densities $p_0$ and $r$, and the current extended target density
is positive, the acceptance probability is
$$1\wedge\frac{p_0(\theta')\widehat L_{\theta'}(U')r(\theta\mid\theta')}{p_0(\theta)\widehat L_\theta(U)r(\theta'\mid\theta)}.$$
Initialize on the extended-target support, where $\pi_0(\theta)>0$ and
$\widehat L_\theta(U)>0$. Proposed zero estimates are rejected. A density-free version uses the
accepted-flow Radon–Nikodym construction in the cited general-state algorithm.
The input is the current extended state $(\theta,U)$; output the proposed
extended state $(\theta',U')$ on acceptance and retain $(\theta,U)$ on
rejection.

The selected path stored in $U$ is part of the auxiliary state. Refreshing its
estimate after rejection defines the different Monte Carlo within Metropolis
procedure, not this algorithm.

Assume AC and the finite-horizon setup of [[def-feynman-kac-path-targets-and-normalizers]] and [[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]]. Fix $N\ge1$ and $t\le T$. Suppose every prefix normalizer satisfies $0<Z_k<\infty$ for $0\le k\le t$. For any nonnegative measurable $\varphi:\mathsf X_{0:t}\to[0,\infty]$ with $\gamma_t(\varphi)<\infty$, define $\widehat\gamma_t^N(\varphi)=\int\varphi\,d(\widehat Z_t\widehat\pi_t^N)$. Then
$$\mathbb E[\widehat\gamma_t^N(\varphi)]=\gamma_t(\varphi).$$
In particular, with $\varphi=1$, the product-of-average-incremental-weights estimator in the algorithm satisfies $\mathbb E[\widehat Z_t]=Z_t$. At each time either multinomial or residual offspring resampling may be used. The theorem asserts no unbiasedness for the normalized empirical measure $\widehat\pi_t^N$ by itself.

Assume AC. The **Metropolis–Hastings procedure** takes as input a standard-Borel
space $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ ([[def-standard-borel-space]]), a target
probability measure $\pi$ ([[def-probability-measure]]), and a probability
kernel $Q$ from $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ to itself
([[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]).

1. On the product sigma-algebra ([[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]),
form the proposal-flow measure $\mu$ ([[def-measure]]) on
$\mathsf X\times\mathsf X$ by
$$\mu(C)=\int_{\mathsf X}Q(x,C_x)\,\pi(dx),\qquad C_x=\{y:(x,y)\in C\}.$$
This is a probability measure by [[lem-prior-and-model-kernel-define-joint-law]].
Let $\tau(x,y)=(y,x)$ and set $\mu^{\mathsf T}(C)=\mu(\tau^{-1}C)$.

2. Set $\eta=\mu\wedge\mu^{\mathsf T}$, the greatest measure dominated by both
flows. Put $\lambda_0=\mu+\mu^{\mathsf T}$, which is a finite measure by
[[thm-nonnegative-weighted-sums-of-measures]], and choose nonnegative measurable
representatives $f=d\mu/d\lambda_0$ and $g=d\mu^{\mathsf T}/d\lambda_0$
with $f+g=1$ everywhere after modification on a $\lambda_0$-null set. Define
$$\alpha(x,y)=\begin{cases}\min\{1,g(x,y)/f(x,y)\},&f(x,y)>0,\\1,&f(x,y)=0.\end{cases}$$
This is a jointly measurable version of $d\eta/d\mu$ taking values in $[0,1]$.

3. For $x\in\mathsf X$, compute the integrated acceptance probability
$$a(x)=\int_{\mathsf X}\alpha(x,y)\,Q(x,dy)$$
and rejection probability $r(x)=1-a(x)$.

4. Return the transition rule
$$P(x,A)=\int_{\mathsf X}\mathbf1_A(y)\alpha(x,y)\,Q(x,dy)+\mathbf1_A(x)r(x),\qquad A\in\mathcal X.$$
The second term retains every rejected proposal as a self-transition.

The item [[lem-common-submeasure-and-bounded-radon-nikodym-density]] proves the
common-submeasure construction and density-version claims in step 2.

Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[alg-metropolis-hastings-kernel]]. Its output
$P$ is a probability kernel, the joint measure
$J_P(dx,dy)=\pi(dx)P(x,dy)$ is symmetric under $(x,y)\mapsto(y,x)$, and $\pi$
is invariant for $P$. Symmetry of this joint measure is reversibility. No
irreducibility, uniqueness, convergence-rate, or central limit theorem
conclusion is asserted.

Let $K$ be a probability kernel on a measurable space $(E,\mathcal E)$
([[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]), and let $\pi$ be a
probability measure on $(E,\mathcal E)$ ([[def-probability-measure]]). The
probability measure $\pi$ is **invariant** for $K$, and $\pi$ is a
**stationary distribution** of $K$, when

$$(\pi K)(A):=\int_E K(x,A)\,\pi(dx)=\pi(A)\qquad\text{for every }A\in\mathcal E .$$

The set function $\pi K$ is again a probability measure: for fixed $A$ the map
$x\mapsto K(x,A)$ is measurable and lies in $[0,1]$, so the integral exists in
$[0,1]$; for pairwise disjoint $A_n\in\mathcal E$ the identity
$K(x,\bigcup_nA_n)=\sum_nK(x,A_n)$ of the measure $K(x,\cdot)$ and the
monotone convergence theorem for nonnegative functions
([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]) give
$\sigma$-additivity of $\pi K$; and $K(x,E)=1$ for every $x$ gives
$(\pi K)(E)=1$. Thus $(\pi K)(A)=\pi(A)$ is an identity between two probability
measures evaluated at $A$.

A $K$-chain whose initial law is $\pi$ is called **stationary** when
$\pi K=\pi$. Stationarity of the process is a statement about all of its
finite-dimensional laws and is proved, not assumed, from $\pi K=\pi$; see
[[thm-invariant-initial-law-makes-the-chain-stationary]].

On a countable state space $E$ with sigma-algebra $2^E$ and transition matrix
$p(x,y)=K(x,\{y\})$ ([[def-transition-matrix-and-n-step-transition-probabilities]]),
a measure on $E$ is its weighted sum of Dirac masses at singletons
([[thm-measures-on-countable-discrete-spaces-are-weighted-dirac-sums]]), so
invariance is equivalent to the matrix identity

$$\pi(y)=\sum_{x\in E}\pi(x)\,p(x,y)\qquad\text{for every }y\in E .$$

The definition fixes no irreducibility, aperiodicity or uniqueness hypothesis,
and it selects no conditional-expectation versions; the display defines a
single measure $\pi K$ and asserts an identity for it. A transient, periodic or
reducible chain may have several invariant probability measures or none.

$$\psi_\theta(du)=\prod_{i=1}^N\nu_{\theta,0}(dx_0^i)\prod_{t=1}^T\prod_{i=1}^N\left[W_{t-1}^{A_t^i}(U)R_{\theta,t}(X_{t-1}^{A_t^i},dx_t^i)\right].$$

The genealogical particle Gibbs extended target is the measure
$$\varphi_N(d\theta,du,k)=C^{-1}\pi_0(d\theta)\,\psi_\theta(du)\,\widehat Z_T(u)W_T^k(u),\qquad k\in\{1,\ldots,N\}.$$
The selected state is $(\theta,X_{0:T}^{K})$. The zero-weight fallback in the
particle algorithm defines $W_T$ everywhere; when $\widehat Z_T=0$ the extended
target assigns the configuration zero mass.

The measure is a probability and has the exact joint smoothing posterior as
its selected $(\theta,X_{0:T}^{K})$ marginal by
[[thm-particle-gibbs-selected-path-marginal]].

For admissible inputs require $\mu_0\ll\nu_0$ and, for each $k\ge1$, $M_k(x,\cdot)\ll R_k(x,\cdot)$ for almost every $x$ under the last-coordinate marginal of the proposal path law $Q_{k-1}$. 1. Draw $X_0^1,\ldots,X_0^N$ independently from $\nu_0$. Set $a_0^i=G_0(X_0^i)\rho_0(X_0^i)$ and $\widehat Z_0=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^Na_0^i$. If $\sum_i a_0^i>0$, put $\bar w_0^i=a_0^i/\sum_j a_0^j$; otherwise put $\bar w_0^i=1/N$. Each initial path is $X_{0:0}^i=X_0^i$.
2. For $k=1,\ldots,t$, do the following:
   1. Apply [[alg-multinomial-and-residual-offspring-resampling]] to the previous normalized weights $(\bar w_{k-1}^1,\ldots,\bar w_{k-1}^N)$, obtaining ancestor indices $A_k^1,\ldots,A_k^N$.
   2. Given the previous paths and these indices, draw $(X_k^1,\ldots,X_k^N)$ with joint conditional law $\bigotimes_{i=1}^N R_k(X_{k-1}^{A_k^i},\cdot)$ and set $X_{0:k}^i=(X_{0:k-1}^{A_k^i},X_k^i)$.
   3. Set $a_k^i=G_k(X_k^i)r_k(X_{k-1}^{A_k^i},X_k^i)$ and $\widehat Z_k=\widehat Z_{k-1}(N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^Na_k^i)$. If $\sum_i a_k^i>0$, put $\bar w_k^i=a_k^i/\sum_j a_k^j$; otherwise put $\bar w_k^i=1/N$.
3. Return $\widehat Z_t$ and the weighted empirical path probability measure $\widehat\pi_t^N=\sum_{i=1}^N\bar w_t^i\delta_{X_{0:t}^i}$. Its last-coordinate marginal is the corresponding empirical filtering approximation.

The all-zero fallback only defines a probability measure for reporting and future sampling. Once a zero average weight occurs, $\widehat Z$ remains zero. The procedure makes no finite-particle accuracy, consistency, or long-time stability claim.

Assume AC and the setup of [[def-feynman-kac-path-targets-and-normalizers]] through a fixed horizon $t\le T$. Let $\nu_0$ be a proposal probability on $\mathsf X_0$, and for $1\le k\le t$ let $R_k:\mathsf X_{k-1}\rightsquigarrow\mathsf X_k$ be proposal probability kernels. Define $Q_s(dx_{0:s})=\nu_0(dx_0)\prod_{k=1}^sR_k(x_{k-1},dx_k)$. Suppose $\mu_0\ll\nu_0$, and for each $k$ suppose $M_k(x,\cdot)\ll R_k(x,\cdot)$ for almost every $x$ under the last-coordinate marginal of $Q_{k-1}$. Choose a measurable version $\rho_0=d\mu_0/d\nu_0$ and, using [[lem-jointly-measurable-radon-nikodym-derivatives-for-probability-kernels]], measurable versions $r_k(x,\cdot)=dM_k(x,\cdot)/dR_k(x,\cdot)$ for these preceding-state marginals.

Then $\gamma_s\ll Q_s$ for every $s\le t$, with product density
$$W_s(x_{0:s})=G_0(x_0)\rho_0(x_0)\prod_{k=1}^sG_k(x_k)r_k(x_{k-1},x_k).$$
That is, $\gamma_s(A)=\int_AW_s\,dQ_s$ for every measurable $A\subseteq\mathsf X_{0:s}$. If $0<Z_s<\infty$, the normalized path target has density $W_s/Z_s$ with respect to $Q_s$.

Assume AC and fix a finite horizon $T\in\mathbb N_0$. For each $0\le k\le T$, let $(\mathsf X_k,\mathcal X_k)$ be a standard Borel space. Let $\mu_0$ be a probability measure on $\mathsf X_0$, and for $1\le k\le T$ let $M_k:\mathsf X_{k-1}\rightsquigarrow\mathsf X_k$ be a probability kernel. A **potential** at time $k$ is a finite-valued nonnegative measurable function $G_k:\mathsf X_k\to[0,\infty)$. Write $\mathsf X_{0:t}=\prod_{k=0}^t\mathsf X_k$ with its finite-product sigma-algebra.

$$\gamma_t(A)=\int_{\mathsf X_{0:t}}\mathbf 1_A(x_{0:t})\prod_{k=0}^tG_k(x_k)\,P_t^M(dx_{0:t}),\qquad A\in\bigotimes_{k=0}^t\mathcal X_k.$$

The selected state is $(\theta,X_{0:T}^{K})$. The zero-weight fallback in the

The measure is a probability and has the exact joint smoothing posterior as

Use the finite-horizon target and proposal setting of [[def-feynman-kac-path-targets-and-normalizers]]. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the finite-horizon Feynman–Kac model and proposal support conditions in
[[def-feynman-kac-path-targets-and-normalizers]] and
[[thm-feynman-kac-path-radon-nikodym-weight]]. Use the multinomial SIR law with ancestor indices in sampled order. Residual resampling is not included in this labeled-density construction. For this variant, additionally
assume that the initial target law has a measurable density $\mu_{\theta,0}$,
each target transition $M_{\theta,t}$ has a jointly measurable density
$f_{\theta,t}(x_t\mid x_{t-1})$, and each proposal transition $R_{\theta,t}$ has
a density $q_{\theta,t}(x_t\mid x_{t-1})$, all with respect to declared
sigma-finite coordinate reference measures. Let $q_{\theta,0}$ be the proposal
initial density with respect to the initial coordinate reference measure.
Retain the proper-prior and positive-finite-evidence assumptions of
[[def-particle-gibbs-extended-target]]. Then
the path measure has density
$$\gamma_{\theta,T}(x_{0:T})=\mu_{\theta,0}(x_0)G_0(x_0)\prod_{t=1}^Tf_{\theta,t}(x_t\mid x_{t-1})G_t(x_t).$$
Require positive finite denominators in the backward probabilities below on
the extended-target support.

Write $U$ for all SIR particles and ancestor indices, $\psi_\theta(u)$ for
their forward joint density, and $j=(j_0,\ldots,j_T)$ for a sequence of
particle indices. Let $x^j_{0:T}$ be the path formed from states
$X_t^{j_t}$, without requiring $A_t^{j_t}=j_{t-1}$. For
$t=0,\ldots,T-1$, define
$$B_t^i(z;U)=\frac{W_t^i f_{\theta,t+1}(z\mid X_t^i)}{\sum_{\ell=1}^NW_t^\ell f_{\theta,t+1}(z\mid X_t^\ell)}.$$
The backward-simulation extended target is
$$\varphi_N^{\rm BS}(d\theta,du,j)=\frac{\pi_0(d\theta)\,\gamma_{\theta,T}(x^j_{0:T})}{C\,N^{T+1}}\frac{\psi_\theta(u)}{q_{\theta,0}(X_0^{j_0})\prod_{t=1}^TW_{t-1}^{A_t^{j_t}}q_{\theta,t}(X_t^{j_t}\mid X_{t-1}^{A_t^{j_t}})}\prod_{t=1}^TB_{t-1}^{A_t^{j_t}}(X_t^{j_t};U).$$
where the displayed expression is a density with respect to the common
particle reference measures, counting measure on ancestor and selected indices,
and the prior measure on $\theta$. The complete SIR forward density
$\psi_\theta$ includes the normalized ancestor probabilities and proposal
densities for every particle. This is the backward-simulation extension of the
particle Gibbs target; its exact selected-path marginal and Gibbs conditionals
are proved in
[[thm-particle-gibbs-backward-simulation-sweep-is-gibbs]].

Use the density, support, and positive-denominator hypotheses of
[[def-particle-gibbs-backward-simulation-extended-target]]. Select multinomial resampling with ancestor indices in sampled order. Fix $N\ge2$. Before updating, require the retained state to be in $D_{\rm BS}$ of [[def-particle-gibbs-backward-simulation-extended-target]]; otherwise return the unchanged retained state. If a required ratio or normalizing sum is undefined, zero or nonfinite during a sweep, return the old retained state. The factorization theorem proves that such failures have conditional probability zero on the designated full-measure set.

A backward-simulation sweep takes the current extended state $(\theta,U,j)$
in $D_{\rm BS}$, where $j=(j_0,\ldots,j_T)$ selects the reference path
$x^*_{0:T}=x^j_{0:T}$ from $U$. It returns the updated extended state $(\theta',U',J)$
and selected path $x^J_{0:T}$. First draw $\theta'$ from its exact posterior
full conditional given $x^*_{0:T}$ and the observations. If
$(\theta',x^*,j)$ is outside $D_{\rm BS}$, return the old extended state.

The initial proposal, non-reference resampling and propagation, and SIR
weight updates use [[alg-conditional-particle-gibbs]] in its density setting.
Because $j$ is a backward index sequence rather than an ancestral lineage, the
reference particle's ancestor is sampled from $B$ below instead of being fixed
to the preceding reference index.

1. Initialize the conditional auxiliary particle filter at time $0$: set
   $X_0^{j_0}=x_0^*$ and independently draw $X_0^i\sim q_{\theta',0}$ for
   $i\ne j_0$. For each $i$, compute the SIR initial weight
   $a_0^i=\mu_{\theta',0}(X_0^i)G_0(X_0^i)/q_{\theta',0}(X_0^i)$. If
   $\sum_i a_0^i>0$, set $W_0^i=a_0^i/\sum_\ell a_0^\ell$; otherwise use the
   SIR zero-weight convention $W_0^i=1/N$.
2. For $t=1,\ldots,T$, do the following in order:
   1. For each $i\ne j_t$, draw $A_t^i$ categorically with probabilities
      $W_{t-1}^{1:N}$ and then draw $X_t^i\sim
      q_{\theta',t}(\cdot\mid X_{t-1}^{A_t^i})$.
   2. Set $X_t^{j_t}=x_t^*$ and draw its ancestor $A_t^{j_t}$ categorically
      with probabilities $B_{t-1}^{1:N}(x_t^*;U')$.
   3. For every $i$, compute
      $a_t^i=G_t(X_t^i)f_{\theta',t}(X_t^i\mid
      X_{t-1}^{A_t^i})/q_{\theta',t}(X_t^i\mid
      X_{t-1}^{A_t^i})$. If $\sum_i a_t^i>0$, set
      $W_t^i=a_t^i/\sum_\ell a_t^\ell$; otherwise use the SIR zero-weight
      convention $W_t^i=1/N$.
3. Draw $J_T$ categorically with probabilities $W_T^{1:N}$. For
   $t=T-1,T-2,\ldots,0$, draw $J_t$ with probabilities
   $B_t^{1:N}(X_{t+1}^{J_{t+1}};U')$. Return the updated extended state and
   selected path.

The zero-weight conventions above define normalized weights as in
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]]. If any required density ratio or
backward-probability denominator is undefined, zero or nonfinite, or a weight
sum is zero or nonfinite, return the old extended state as specified above.
On the designated good set these exceptional events have conditional
probability zero. For $T=0$, Step 2 is empty and Step 3 draws $J_0$ from $W_0$.

The conditional auxiliary particle filter and the backward simulator are the
two particle-coordinate conditionals of
[[def-particle-gibbs-backward-simulation-extended-target]]. Their Gibbs
interpretation and exact posterior marginal are separate proved properties.

Choose a measurable version $\rho_0=d\mu_0/d\nu_0$ and, using [[lem-jointly-measurable-radon-nikodym-derivatives-for-probability-kernels]], measurable versions $r_k(x,\cdot)=dM_k(x,\cdot)/dR_k(x,\cdot)$ for these preceding-state marginals.

Then $\gamma_s\ll Q_s$ for every $s\le t$, with product density
$$W_s(x_{0:s})=G_0(x_0)\rho_0(x_0)\prod_{k=1}^sG_k(x_k)r_k(x_{k-1},x_k).$$
That is, $\gamma_s(A)=\int_AW_s\,dQ_s$ for every measurable $A\subseteq\mathsf X_{0:s}$. If $0<Z_s<\infty$, the normalized path target has density $W_s/Z_s$ with respect to $Q_s$.

Assume AC and fix a finite horizon $T\in\mathbb N_0$. For each $0\le k\le T$, let $(\mathsf X_k,\mathcal X_k)$ be a standard Borel space. Let $\mu_0$ be a probability measure on $\mathsf X_0$, and for $1\le k\le T$ let $M_k:\mathsf X_{k-1}\rightsquigarrow\mathsf X_k$ be a probability kernel. A **potential** at time $k$ is a finite-valued nonnegative measurable function $G_k:\mathsf X_k\to[0,\infty)$. Write $\mathsf X_{0:t}=\prod_{k=0}^t\mathsf X_k$ with its finite-product sigma-algebra.

For each $0\le t\le T$, let $P_t^M$ be the finite path law with ordered kernel integral $\mu_0(dx_0)\prod_{k=1}^tM_k(x_{k-1},dx_k)$, supplied by Ionescu–Tulcea ([[thm-ionescu-tulcea-construction-of-a-markov-chain]]). The **unnormalized Feynman–Kac path measure** is
$$\gamma_t(A)=\int_{\mathsf X_{0:t}}\mathbf 1_A(x_{0:t})\prod_{k=0}^tG_k(x_k)\,P_t^M(dx_{0:t}),\qquad A\in\bigotimes_{k=0}^t\mathcal X_k.$$
Its **normalizer** is $Z_t=\gamma_t(\mathsf X_{0:t})=\gamma_t(1)\in[0,\infty]$. Only when $0<Z_t<\infty$ define the normalized path target $\pi_t^{\mathrm{FK}}=\gamma_t/Z_t$. The sequence $(\gamma_t)$ with its kernels and potentials is the Feynman–Kac flow.

State-space filtering kernels are conditional-law versions as in [[def-state-space-filtering-laws]]. A Feynman–Kac path target is not by itself an assertion that a pointwise conditional version has been selected at observation-null histories.

$$w_t(z,X_{t-1}^i)=w_t(z,X_{t-1}^\ell)\frac{f_t(z\mid X_{t-1}^i)q_t(z\mid X_{t-1}^\ell)}{f_t(z\mid X_{t-1}^\ell)q_t(z\mid X_{t-1}^i)}.$$

a prior probability $\pi_0$, and the finite-horizon Feynman–Kac path model in
[[def-feynman-kac-path-targets-and-normalizers]]. Write
$$L_\theta(y_{1:T})=\gamma_{\theta,T}(1),\qquad C=\int_\Theta L_\theta(y_{1:T})\,\pi_0(d\theta).$$
Require every prefix normalizer $0<Z_{\theta,t}<\infty$ for $t=0,\ldots,T$
and $\pi_0$-almost every $\theta$, together with $0<C<\infty$; then the
parameter posterior is
$$\pi_y(d\theta)=C^{-1}L_\theta(y_{1:T})\,\pi_0(d\theta).$$

For fixed particle count $N\ge1$, let $U$ contain the full output of
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]] at $\theta$ and a terminal index
$K\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$ drawn conditionally with its final normalized weight.
Let $m_\theta(du)$ be this measurable auxiliary-variable probability kernel and
let $\widehat L_\theta(U)=\widehat Z_T$ be jointly measurable and nonnegative
in $(\theta,U)$. The required interface is
$$\int\widehat L_\theta(u)\,m_\theta(du)=L_\theta(y_{1:T});$$
[[thm-sequential-particle-estimator-is-unbiased]] supplies this identity under
its finite-horizon support and integrability hypotheses. Define the extended
target probability by
$$\widetilde\pi(d\theta,du)=C^{-1}\pi_0(d\theta)m_\theta(du)\widehat L_\theta(u).$$

Given current $(\theta,U)$, propose $\theta'\sim R(\theta,\cdot)$ and then
$U'\sim m_{\theta'}$. Apply the general Metropolis–Hastings construction
[[alg-metropolis-hastings-kernel]] to this proposal kernel and target
$\widetilde\pi$. On rejection retain the entire current pair $(\theta,U)$,
including its stored likelihood estimate and selected path index. When $\pi_0$
and $R$ have densities $p_0$ and $r$, and the current extended target density
is positive, the acceptance probability is
$$1\wedge\frac{p_0(\theta')\widehat L_{\theta'}(U')r(\theta\mid\theta')}{p_0(\theta)\widehat L_\theta(U)r(\theta'\mid\theta)}.$$
Initialize on the extended-target support, where $\pi_0(\theta)>0$ and
$\widehat L_\theta(U)>0$. Proposed zero estimates are rejected. A density-free version uses the
accepted-flow Radon–Nikodym construction in the cited general-state algorithm.
The input is the current extended state $(\theta,U)$; output the proposed
extended state $(\theta',U')$ on acceptance and retain $(\theta,U)$ on
rejection.

The selected path stored in $U$ is part of the auxiliary state. Refreshing its

Under the hypotheses of [[alg-pmmh]], assume the unbiasedness identity there

probability measure whose parameter marginal is $\pi_y$. With the terminal

parameter and selected-path marginals are therefore exact for every fixed

uniqueness, convergence rate, or mixing speed.
